pages.text: "Go away! Noisy!" Dari shouted at Kkiruk on the shore rocks. He wanted to count a row of shells quietly, but the gull kept calling. Kkiruk repeated his words exactly.
Dari spoke more sharply. "I don't like you! Go away!" Kkiruk returned the same words. Dari's heart stung, and his counting flipper stopped.
"Silly!" Dari shouted. "Silly!" Kkiruk replied, then flew to the roof. Alone on the rocks, Dari drooped his flippers. "Why keep saying that to me...?"
Mom came from hanging seaweed and sat beside him. "How would 'I don't like you' feel?" Dari thought. "Really upsetting..."
Mom smiled. "Kkiruk returns what they hear. Sharp words bring sharp words. Kind words bring kind words!" Dari lifted his head. "I spoke sharply first!"
Mom raised her flippers one by one. "One, think first! Two, choose kind words! 'Let's play' instead of 'Go away.' 'Lovely song' instead of 'Noisy.'" Dari practiced.
Kkiruk landed again. Dari smiled. "Sorry about before. Let's play!" Kkiruk repeated, "Sorry about before. Let's play!" Kind words bring kind words!
Kkiruk brought a shiny shell in their beak and laid it before Dari. "Thank you!" Dari said. "Thank you!" came back. Dari slapped his tail happily.
Now Dari took three steps before speaking. "One, think first! Two, choose kind words! Three, remember thank you and sorry!" He and Kkiruk lined up shells together.
Mom touched her nose to his. "Kind words made Kkiruk smile!" Kind words came back kind, sharp words came back sharp. "Kind words bring kind words!" Kkiruk echoed from the roof.
